newsitem.title: USA: Georgia-Pacific Q1 market similar to Q4.
newsitem.headline: Georgia-Pacific Q1 market similar to Q4.

text.p: Pulp and paper company Georgia-Pacific Corp said Thursday that market conditions during the first quarter remained "very similar" to those of the fourth quarter of 1996.
The company reported earnings of $0.99 a share for the first quarter, against $0.55 a year ago.

"In pulp and containerboard, industry inventories increased in the quarter and prices declined," it said. "While demand for our communication papers increased, we experienced a severe decline in earnings due to lower prices than a year ago.
"The bright spot in pulp and paper continues to be our tissue business. Prices remain strong, as does profitability."
Georgia-Pacific said lumber and gypsum operations continued to post outstanding results, plywood prices increased, but oriented strand board prices remained very weak due to excess industry capacity.
"Overall, our building products manufacturing business reported operating profits more than double those of a year ago and up 25 percent from the 1996 fourth quarter," it said.

"While our distribution division again reported a disappointing loss, the group is fully focused on its aggressive plan to return to profitability," it said. "This would result in a significant profit and cash flow swing in this business."
